In light of the concerns regarding AI safety, I created a website to track all known cases of misalignment.

Frontier labs should make all misalignment data public. Citizens have a right to transparency, especially when public policy decisions are being made. Let's all get aligned on the misalignment so we can make data-driven decisions in a democratic fashion.

- Alex Wormuth

story_text.value:
I wanted to re-play SimTower but found it too difficult to get running through emulation. Instead, I worked for 6 months with Claude Code on a complete rewrite, replicating all the functionality from a Ghidra decompilation of the binary, an AI-generated summary of the original source code and my memory of the gameplay. Then deployed it to the web as WASM.

I wanted the original feel of the game, so didn't create new art. Instead, you load an original binary you provide, and the on-page code parses it and pulls out the original assets.

I didn't look at a single line of code Claude wrote, but spent hours playing through the game and nitpicking every little behavior. A lot of time was spent convincing myself that the elevators just ARE that hard to get right >.<

I hope everyone can enjoy this game again. Did a writeup here: https://www.wyldcard.io/blog/simtower-remake-playable-in-bro...

source: https://github.com/Jonahss/concilia-tower

story_text.value:
Hey y’all!

Back in 2019, inspired by my love of board games and what’s possible with digital games, I created a little strategy game built around simultaneous moves and shifting pressure across a grid. I thought there was a really interesting game hiding in there, but eventually stopped digging as life happened. Work, pandemic, kid, the usual...

Then all of this AI nonsense pulled me back in and made me want to see how far I could run with the original idea. That turned into Ember, which somehow also became my first app ever on the App Store and Google Play.

I haven’t had this much fun building something since I was a kid. Hope some of you enjoy it!

story_text.value:
Hi HN! A few friends and I built EarthToPixels, a project that turns real-world cities into explorable pixel-art maps.

We fine-tuned an open-source Qwen image model and built a pipeline that takes aerial imagery, generates pixel-art tiles, and keeps neighboring generations visually continuous so they can be stitched into a large map.

We built the pipeline to work with arbitrary coordinates rather than a specific city. For the first complete render, we chose our hometown: João Pessoa, Brazil. You can explore it here: https://earthtopixels.com/

Would love to hear what you think, especially about the technical side.

title.value: Show HN: EarthToPixels – Turning real cities into explorable pixel art

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

I'm Chinedu, the creator of Lynen

I built this because I got tired of buying clothes and having the seams pull out after the first wash or purchasing garments that said 100% cotton and turns out there is some polyester or toxic dye in the composition.

Key Features

1. Mobile App - You can take this with you anywhere.

2. Scan or Search - Scan or manually look garment barcode and get lab verified fabric and chemical composition of your garment, as well as a durability result.

3. Personalization - A virtual assistant that provides tailored analysis from your skin notes. Helps makes better decisions when shopping.

Tech Stack

Built this using Next.js, React with TypeScript & TailwindCSS for styling, and Supabase for database

Why I'm Posting Now

I'm building a waitlist for the app launch which is in the coming days. I would love to build some traction before that happens.

title.value: Show HN: Lynen – A mobile app that tells you what clothes are made from

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

I just hit a major milestone on my side project.

I work a demanding day job, so I built a platform where Stockfish plays continuous self-play (2s/move to keep server load manageable) to analyze asymmetrical chess variants.

In Chess960v2, White and Black independently choose any of the 960 valid setups, resulting in 921,600 possible starting combinations. I'm running a massive round-robin tournament (960 rounds total, where each setup plays against every other setup), and 600 out of 960 rounds have been completed.

The goal is to mathematically find which combinations are genuinely balanced (50/50) and which give an unfair engine bias to one side due to asymmetry.

I'm pretty exhausted today, so I might be slow to reply, but I'd love for you to check out the site, look at the current data, and share your thoughts.

Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: Chess960v2.com – 960×960 asymmetric chess, 600/960 rounds done

story_text.value:
For fun, I wrote a c compiler (non-optimizing) in Java targeting modern C (C23) using claude. I developed a c shell similar to jshell in java. The compiler also bundles a built in an assembler for x86. A linker is planned for end-to-end compilation. There is still a lot of work in progress but I wanted to share the project early for feedback. I spent around $400 in AI credits so far and it took over a week on and off of working on it.

I drive the architecture of the compiler and verify the AI implementation with a large test suite.

It can compile and run lua (all test passing) and curl (partially).

Cheers!

story_text.value:
I wrote a screenplay a couple years ago and decided to see if I could actually “film it” with AI video tools. Deviant is the result, an 84 minute sci-fi thriller about a tech mogul's clone that finds an exploit in its own safety code.
The process: Character and set reference images in Midjourney and Nano Banana. Scene by scene prompts written from the script (I have an agent skill now for this), generated in Google Veo for most of the film, until it stopped working reliably, then I shelved it. Now with Seedance 2.5 available in the US on Higgsfield, I completed the final act. The last 20 minutes look noticeably better than the first 60.
Edited just in iMovie, audio with ElevenLabs.
I decided to release it as is rather than regenerate everything. Biggest problems were getting the actors to “act”, shot composition, character consistency, voice matching, and getting more than two characters to interact coherently in one frame. Happy to go into detail on any of it.

title.value: Show HN: Deviant, a feature-length sci-fi thriller about AI, made with AI
